question: What is the primary focus of medical services for special children?

options.B: Meeting the unique developmental and physical needs of children with disabilities
options.C: Managing surgical emergencies in school-aged children
options.D: Treating only acute infectious diseases in hospitals

explanation: These specialized services focus on children who require extra medical, physical, or developmental support beyond standard care. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why do special children typically require care that goes beyond routine pediatric visits?

options.A: Standard pediatric clinics do not admit children with chronic illnesses
options.B: They have complex developmental, physical, or chronic health conditions
options.C: Special children only need care during emergency situations
options.D: Routine checkups are completely unnecessary after the first year of life

explanation: Their unique health profiles demand coordinated, specialized interventions rather than standard checkups alone. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h1)

question: What is developmental surveillance during routine clinic visits?

options.B: Testing blood sugar levels every morning
options.D: Ongoing informal observation of child milestones

explanation: Surveillance is the continuous process where nurses and doctors watch for expected developmental milestones during routine contacts. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h2)

question: A nurse notices a toddler has not started walking or babbling by the expected age. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Tell the parents to wait until the child turns five years old
options.C: Refer the child for formal developmental screening and evaluation
options.D: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics for a suspected infection

explanation: Missed milestones should prompt formal screening to catch potential delays early and start interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of a comprehensive pediatric assessment after a positive screening?

options.A: To establish a clear diagnosis and guide treatment planning
options.B: To replace the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: To prove that developmental delays are always temporary
options.D: To discharge the patient from the healthcare system permanently

explanation: A thorough assessment provides the specific medical and developmental diagnosis needed to build an effective care plan. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why is the nursing history an essential part of a comprehensive assessment?

options.A: It provides vital details about the child's developmental timeline and home environment
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory investigations
options.C: It diagnoses rare genetic disorders without testing
options.D: It is only used for billing and insurance purposes

explanation: Parents share daily observations that help nurses and doctors understand the full picture of the child's health. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which professional primarily helps a special child improve fine motor skills for daily tasks like dressing and eating?
explanation: Occupational therapists focus on upper body function and fine motor tasks needed for everyday independence. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team approach essential for children with complex special needs?

options.A: It allows a single nurse to perform all surgical procedures
options.B: It eliminates the need for any parental involvement in home care
options.C: It ensures all physical, developmental, and emotional aspects are managed by experts
options.D: It reduces the total number of hospital visits to exactly one per year

explanation: Complex conditions require diverse skills from different specialists to cover every aspect of the child's health and development. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of rehabilitation services for special children?

options.A: To keep the child confined to a hospital bed
options.B: To eliminate the need for any assistive technology
options.C: To completely cure all genetic and congenital disorders
options.D: To maximize independence and improve quality of life

explanation: Rehabilitation focuses on helping children function at their highest possible level despite chronic limitations. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h5)

question: A nurse is teaching a mother how to support her child with cerebral palsy at home. What is the most important nursing action?

options.A: Discourage the child from participating in play activities
options.B: Encourage consistent daily exercises and proper use of prescribed braces
options.C: Advise the mother to stop all therapy sessions once the child starts school
options.D: Tell the family to avoid using any mobility assistive devices

explanation: Consistency at home with therapy routines and assistive devices is vital for maintaining physical gains. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a major advantage of community-based rehabilitation programs in Nigeria?

options.A: They provide high-cost neurosurgeries in every primary health center
options.B: They bring essential therapy and support services closer to rural families
options.C: They completely replace the need for tertiary medical centers
options.D: They eliminate cultural beliefs regarding disabilities

explanation: Community-based programs bridge the gap for families who cannot easily travel to major city hospitals. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by nurses providing community care for special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of well-funded pediatric specialists in rural clinics

explanation: Rural areas actually suffer from a severe shortage of specialists, making this option untrue. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is the core philosophy of family-centered care in pediatrics?

options.A: Viewing the family as an essential partner in the child's healthcare
options.C: Excluding family members from daily medical decisions
options.D: Treating the child without input from the parents

explanation: Family-centered care builds on the strengths of families and honors their central role in the child's life. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: Why is educating parents about their child's chronic condition so important?

options.A: It prevents the child from ever growing up
options.B: It turns parents into licensed medical doctors
options.C: It empowers them to provide safe daily care and advocate for their child
options.D: It ensures the parents never need to visit a clinic again

explanation: Well-informed parents can manage home routines effectively and speak up for their child's needs in healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h7)

question: What is a major financial barrier for families of special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory free private nursing care at home
options.B: Excessive government funding for all childhood treatments
options.C: Free international travel for medical checkups
options.D: High out-of-pocket costs for therapies and medical supplies

explanation: Most families bear the financial burden of care directly because public insurance coverage for chronic disabilities is limited. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h8)

question: What is the primary role of nurses regarding disability policy frameworks?

options.A: To penalize families who miss therapy appointments
options.B: To advocate for policy enforcement and connect families with support resources
options.C: To write and pass new national constitutions
options.D: To collect taxes for hospital construction

explanation: Nurses act as patient advocates, helping families access rights and benefits guaranteed under existing laws. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h8)
